Ex. Ord. No. 9158. Air Medal
Ex. Ord. No. 9158, May 11, 1942, 7 F.R. 3541, as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 9242–A, Sept. 11, 1942, 7 F.R. 7874; Ex. Ord. No. 14085, § 1, Oct. 3, 2022, 87 F.R. 60541, provided:

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole clause is the order as a whole: the establishment of the Air Medal, the design-approval and award authority, and the one-medal rule with bars or devices and posthumous presentation. It was not terminated by any held instrument. Executive Order 9242-A restated the first paragraph and Executive Order 14085 further amended the first and second paragraphs and added a final paragraph; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, and both amendments are recorded as later events with the text before and after. The held U.S. Code note prints the order as amended on a release point current through 2026-10-09 with no ending statement, no held source revokes or supersedes the order, and the order has no duration or condition of its own, so the clause was operative on 2026-10-14.

later_events.mechanism: amendment (restatement of the first paragraph): before, the first paragraph described service in any capacity in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard; after, it describes service in any capacity in or with those forces; the rest of the paragraph (establishment of the Air Medal with ribbons, date of September 8, 1939, meritorious achievement while participating in an aerial flight) is repeated unchanged

later_events.mechanism: amendment (strike and insert, with a new final paragraph): first paragraph, before: Army and Navy, any person, distinguishes or has distinguished himself, forces listed without the Air Force and Space Force; after: Armed Forces, those individuals, distinguish or have distinguished themselves, Air Force and Space Force added; second paragraph, before: design approved by the Secretaries of War, the Navy and the Treasury and award by those Secretaries, and Coast Guard awards under the Navy's jurisdiction; after: design approved by the Secretary of Defense, award by the Secretaries of the Army, the Navy, the Air Force or the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, and Coast Guard awards under the jurisdiction of the Navy; new final paragraph: regulations of the Secretaries of the military departments on the award shall be uniform so far as practicable and subject to the approval of the Secretary of Defense. Reviewer note: the substance of the second paragraph's award authority changed, while the establishment of the medal and the one-medal rule continue

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me  
as President of the United States and as  
Commander in Chief of the Army and  
Navy of the United States, it is hereby  
ordered that an Air Medal, with accom­
panying ribbons, be established for  
award to any person who, while serving  
in any capacity in the Army, Navy, Ma­
rine Corps, or Coast Guard of the United  
States subsequent to September 8, 1939,  
distinguishes, or has distinguished, him­
self by meritorious achievement while  
participating in an aerial flight.
The Air Medal and appurtenances  
thereto shall 'be of appropriate design  
approved by the Secretary of War, the  
Secretary of the Navy, and the Secre­
tary of the Treasury, and, under such  
regulations as said Secretaries may pre­
scribe, may be awarded by the Secretary  
of War, the Secretary of the Navy, or the  
Secretary of the Treasury, or by such  
commanding officers of the Army, Navy,  
Marine Corps, or Coast Guard as the  
said Secretaries may respectively desig­
nate. Awards to personnel of the Coast  
Guard when serving under his jurisdic­
tion shall be made by or under the direc­
tion of the Secretary of the Navy.
No more than one Air Medal shall be  
awarded to any one person, but for each  
succeeding meritorious achievement jus­
tifying such an award a suitable bar or  
other device may be awarded to be worn  
with the medal as prescribed by appro­
priate regulations. In the event of a  
posthumous award the medal, bar, or  
device may be presented to such repre­
sentative of the deceased as may be  
designated in the award.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register original (7 FR 3541, PDF page 1; text file EO_9158 of the fr-originals job) is Executive Order 9158, Air Medal, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt on May 11, 1942 (F. R. Doc. 42-4314, filed May 12, 1942); the number, title and date agree with the register row. The order has one inventory clause covering its three paragraphs. Two held later instruments amend the order and neither ends it. Executive Order 9242-A (signed September 11, 1942; 7 FR 7874) restated the first paragraph so that service in or with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard qualifies. Executive Order 14085 section 1 (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541) further amended the first and second paragraphs by striking and inserting words (Armed Forces, Air Force and Space Force, those individuals, approval of the design by the Secretary of Defense, award by the Secretaries of the Army, the Navy and the Air Force or the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, and Coast Guard personnel serving under the jurisdiction of the Navy) and added a final paragraph on uniform regulations. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, and each amendment is a later event that records the text before and after. Current law: the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (Office of the Law Revision Counsel release point 119-121, edition current through 2026-10-09) prints the order as amended by both instruments and states no ending; the order has no duration, condition or sunset of its own. Route original_plus_bounded_search: the held original, both held later instruments, no own-terms end, and the three bounded searches after reading their coverage notes. The U.S. Code search found one hit, the note above; its edition ends 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected, which is disclosed here and is not a ground to doubt a presidential order that no held source ends. The eCFR search (point in time as of 2026-10-14) found no hit. The Federal Register catalog notes held for this order are an Amended-by note naming EO 9242-A, a See note naming Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948 (13 FR 8163), and the Amends note under EO 14085; none is a revocation or supersession. The order was unrevoked and operative on 2026-10-14.

The only instruments that name the order are Executive Order 9242-A and Executive Order 14085 (both amendments), later reprints and regulations that cite it as amended (the 1948 and 1954 Federal Register concordance pages and the 2022 Federal Register copy), and the catalog See note to Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948, a cross-reference whose text is not held and which no held source describes as an ending. Executive Order 14085 amended the order in 2022, after that transfer order, and the Code note prints the order after both. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole clause is the restatement of the first paragraph of Executive Order 9158 so that the Air Medal may be awarded for service in or with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard. No held instrument revoked or superseded it. Executive Order 14085 section 1(a) further amended the same paragraph by striking and inserting words but did not strike the words in or with that Executive Order 9242-A added; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, and the later amendment is recorded as a later event with the text before and after. The held U.S. Code note prints Executive Order 9158 as amended by Executive Order 9242-A with no ending statement on a release point current through 2026-10-09, so the clause was operative on 2026-10-14. Reviewer note: this is an amending clause whose wording is carried inside the parent order's text.

later_events.mechanism: amendment (strike and insert) of the first paragraph that Executive Order 9242-A restated: before, Army and Navy, any person, distinguishes or has distinguished himself, and the forces listed as Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard; after, Armed Forces, those individuals, distinguish or have distinguished themselves, and Air Force and Space Force added to the forces listed; the words in or with, added by Executive Order 9242-A, are not struck

source.quote:
Executive Order 9158 
of May 11, 1942 (Air Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9242–A 
of September 11, 1942 (Amending Executive Order No. 9158 of May 11, 
1942, to Provide that the Air Medal May Be Awarded to Persons Serving 
with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard of the United States), 
is further amended as follows: 
(a) The first paragraph is amended— 
(i) by striking ‘‘Army and Navy’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘Armed 
Forces’’; 
(ii) by striking ‘‘any person’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘those individ-
uals’’; 
(iii) by inserting ‘‘Air Force, Space Force,’’ after ‘‘Marine Corps,’’; and 
(iv) by striking ‘‘distinguishes, or has distinguished, himself’’ and inserting 
in lieu thereof ‘‘distinguish, or have distinguished, themselves’’.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me as President of the United States and 
as Commander in Chief of the Army and 
Navy of the United States, it is hereby 
ordered that the first paragraph of Ex­
ecutive Order No. 9158 of May, 11, 1942,1  
establishing the Air Medal, be, and it is 
hereby amended to read as follows:
“By virtue of the authority vested in 
me as President of the United States and 
as Commander in Chief of the Army and 
Navy of the United States, it is hereby or­
dered that an Air Medal, with accom­
panying ribbons, be established for award 
to any person who, while serving in any 
capacity in or with the Army, Navy, M a­
rine Corps, or Coast Guard of the United 
States, subsequent to September 8, 1939, 
distinguishes, or has distinguished, him­
self by meritorious achievement while 
participating in an aerial flight.”

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text for 7 FR 7874 (PDF page 4 of the issue of 1942-10-06; text file EO_9242A of the fr-originals job) contains, at characters 1535 to 2383, the heading Executive Order 9242-A, Amending Executive Order No. 9158 of May 11, 1942, to provide that the Air Medal may be awarded to persons serving with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt at The White House on September 11, 1942 (F. R. Doc. 42-9873, filed October 3, 1942); the number, title and date agree with the register row. Inventory correction: that held text begins with the closing items of the preceding order (Executive Order 9242), so the draft inventory (items 6 and 7, characters 556 to 1143) describes a different order and is replaced by one clause, the operative text of Executive Order 9242-A, which has a single operative paragraph restating the first paragraph of Executive Order 9158. The restated paragraph differs from the original first paragraph of Executive Order 9158 by adding that the service may be in or with the named forces. Executive Order 14085 section 1(a) (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541) further amended that same first paragraph by striking and inserting words (Armed Forces, those individuals, Air Force and Space Force, distinguish themselves) and did not strike the words that Executive Order 9242-A added, so the amendment's wording is carried in the current text. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended; the later amendment is recorded as a later event with the text before and after. Reviewer note: the clause is an amending clause whose effect is carried inside the parent order's first paragraph, and Executive Order 14085 rewrote other words of that paragraph. Current law: the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (Office of the Law Revision Counsel release point 119-121, edition current through 2026-10-09) prints Executive Order 9158 as amended by Executive Order 9242-A and Executive Order 14085 and states no ending. Route original_plus_bounded_search: the held original, the held later instrument, no own-terms end, and the three bounded searches after reading their coverage notes. The U.S. Code search found one hit, the note above, and its edition ends 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected; the eCFR search (point in time as of 2026-10-14) found no hit; the Federal Register catalog notes held for the order are the Amends note under Executive Order 9242-A naming Executive Order 9158, a See note naming Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948 (13 FR 8163), and the Amends note under Executive Order 14085; none is a revocation or supersession of Executive Order 9242-A. The order was unrevoked and its amendment remained in the operative text of Executive Order 9158 on 2026-10-14.
